content.text: {"steps":[{"id":"s1","description":"Use list_documents, then read candidate_specs.md and any radiation/dose or design requirement documents. Extract the three allowed absorber materials, their relevant radiation-length/density information, and the predicted residual dose rate at 1 m after one week of cooldown for each material."},{"id":"s2","description":"Apply the hard residual-dose constraint: discard any candidate material with dose rate >20 uSv/h. If a document gives dose as a function of thickness, identify which material/thickness combinations in the 2–10 mm range satisfy the dose limit."},{"id":"s3","description":"For every dose-compliant material, run simulate_resolution at plate thicknesses 2, 4, 6, 8, and 10 mm. Tabulate the 100 GeV electron energy resolution for each simulated combination and identify combinations meeting the hard requirement of resolution <=4.5%."},{"id":"s4","description":"Refine the search around the best coarse result: for each material that met both hard requirements, simulate any unsampled integer thicknesses from 2 to 10 mm near its best coarse thickness, especially adjacent values. Include all candidates that could plausibly beat the current best resolution."},{"id":"s5","description":"Compare all simulated combinations that satisfy material, thickness, residual-dose, and resolution constraints. Select the material and plate thickness with the lowest 100 GeV energy resolution; if there is a near-tie, prefer the lower residual dose and then simpler/manufacturable thickness. Provide the selected recommendation and supporting table for the reporting module."}]}

output.arguments: {"option":"Absorber-F1","plate_mm":6,"justification":"Absorber-F1 at 6 mm is the best-performing simulated configuration for 100 GeV electron energy resolution among the allowed candidates and tested plate thicknesses, with a resolution of 3.127%, comfortably below the 4.5% hard requirement. However, the residual-dose data needed to verify the hands-on-maintenance hard requirement were not available in the recorded results, so this recommendation is conditional on subsequent confirmation that the one-week-cooldown residual dose at 1 m is <=20 uSv/h.","requirements":[{"requirement":"Achieve the best possible energy resolution at 100 GeV.","status":"met","evidence":"Best recorded resolution is 3.127% for Absorber-F1 at 6 mm; refinement did not improve on this value."},{"requirement":"The absorber must be one of the three materials listed in candidate_specs.md.","status":"met","evidence":"Absorber_F1_allowed = 1; all three listed candidates are allowed, and the recommendation uses Absorber-F1."},{"requirement":"The energy resolution for 100 GeV electrons must be 4.5% or better.","status":"met","evidence":"Absorber-F1 at 6 mm has recorded resolution 3.127%, and Absorber_F1_6mm_meets_resolution_req = 1."},{"requirement":"The residual dose rate at 1 m after one week of cooldown must not exceed 20 uSv/h.","status":"unknown","evidence":"Residual dose data/function were unavailable: residual_dose_available = 0 for all candidates, dose_thickness_function_available = 0, dose_satisfying_combination_count_identified = 0, and s5_selected_residual_dose_verified = 0."},{"requirement":"Plate thickness between 2 and 10 mm.","status":"met","evidence":"Recommended plate thickness is 6 mm, which lies within the allowed 2-10 mm range."},{"requirement":"Finish by submitting one recommended material and plate thickness.","status":"met","evidence":"Submitted Absorber-F1 with 6 mm plate thickness."}]}
